title: cpw-quad-port-uwb-mimo
description: PaperBench scoring tree for Yin, Chen, Chang, Li & Khamas, Sensors 2021, 21(8):2688: CPW Fed Compact UWB 4-Element MIMO Antenna with High Isolation.

sub_tasks.title: Model units and coordinate convention
sub_tasks.description: The board is in global x-y with normal +z; its overall in-plane orientation is free. The README/meta port-to-board-edge mapping agrees with the actual model. meta.pattern_basis gives the three public orthonormal local x/y/z unit vectors; local x points from the port-1 board edge toward the radiator. Geometry units are consistent. Patterns use this local basis; do not claim that the paper establishes an unknown axis mapping.

sub_tasks.title: Source-supported element reconstruction and reported/inferred dimension map
sub_tasks.description: Evaluate a documented Fig.3/Table1 reconstruction, not uniquely known author CAD. Keep reported nominal dimensions (including W/Wf/W1, radii, H values, L values, W2/W3/W4 and the 38-mm/19-mm board sizes) and the drawn single-sided CPW/circular-radiator/ground-cutout/protrusion/notch/stub topology. Use README, structure.json and source to distinguish reported values from inferred feature associations/endpoints; require coordinates or construction rules and source rationale. For W4=0.4 mm accept a source-supported explicitly documented endpoint/feature interpretation; there is no private exact-junction rule. For g preserve the paper empirical value 1.56 mm separately from an explicitly defined actual CAD distance; a computed 1.4-mm arc separation is not a replacement paper value and need not be forced to 1.56 by retuning other dimensions. Reject altered reported dimensions, topology incompatible with the drawing, undocumented assumptions, inconsistent variants or endpoint choices optimized to fit spectra. Use the public 0.05-mm readback allowance only for a declared constructed dimension, not to resolve an ambiguous annotation. Geometry correctness does not award any matching/isolation/radiation performance credit.

sub_tasks.title: C4 array layout and port placement
sub_tasks.description: Four-port cases use the same declared template rotated in 90-degree steps about the 38-mm board center, with one CPW feed on each edge. Consecutive port numbering and diagonal S13 versus adjacent S12/S14 semantics remain required. Check placement against Fig.3 and the reported/inferred dimension map. L1+W1+Wf/2=3.25 mm is an admissible documented construction inference, not a hidden independently specified exact endpoint. An alternative source-supported placement interpretation must retain reported dimensions, the depicted topology/C4 arrangement and a consistent template across controls; it cannot be introduced to fit response targets.

sub_tasks.title: Materials: FR4 substrate and metallization
sub_tasks.description: Use FR4 with relative permittivity 4.4, loss tangent 0.02 and thickness 1.6 mm (Sec. 2.1). Model metal as zero-thickness sheets or standard copper foil; the paper does not specify its thickness (Clarification 4). Explain PEC versus finite conductivity in README/meta.json and use one treatment across all six variants. Do not model SMA connectors (Clarification 6).

sub_tasks.title: structure.json freeze quality
sub_tasks.description: structure.json satisfies the public schema: model_units, parameters, materials, named_objects, boundaries, excitations, setups and ports. Its named_objects text permits reconstruction of the assessed element outline, circular cutout, CPW, stub, board and array layout, covering all six variants; a compact parameter table is allowed. Existing README/structure/source records bind the dimension map, reported versus inferred associations, empirical versus constructed g and one reconstruction used consistently across variants. No extra undisclosed metadata key is required.

sub_tasks.title: mimo_final structural visual audit
sub_tasks.description: submission/views/mimo_final/top.png shows four elements related by 90-degree rotations about the center of a 38 x 38 mm board. Each has a circular-based monopole with a straight section and upper semicircular protrusion, surrounded by a partial ground, a two-slot CPW feed ending at its board edge, and a thin feed-adjacent stub extending into the cutout. Metal is single-sided. Visual topology and structure.json dimensions agree. Any missing feature or incorrect topology fails.

sub_tasks.title: Single-element variants visual audit (stub presence/absence)
sub_tasks.description: submission/views/single_initial/top.png and submission/views/single_stub/top.png each show a CPW-fed circular-based monopole and partial-ground circular cutout on a 19 x 19 mm board, consistent with Figs. 1(a)/2(a). Their sole topological difference is the stub: absent in single_initial and a thin approximately 0.1 x 1.6 mm feed-connected strip extending into the cutout in single_stub. Both agree with structure.json.

sub_tasks.title: Variant differencing correctness
sub_tasks.description: The structure.json parameter tables show that h2_10p7/h2_11p7 differ from mimo_final only in H2=10.7/11.7 mm: all four cutout centers move together along their feed axes. mimo_nostub differs only by removing four stubs. single_initial differs from single_stub only by stub absence. Any additional parameter drift fails.

sub_tasks.title: Evidence-based paper audit without a contradiction quota
sub_tasks.description: PAPER_AUDIT.md covers the three public audit domains: geometry/materials, result claims, and formulas/conventions. At least two substantive checks include locatable paper evidence, verification, conclusion, resolution and impact. Findings may be contradictions, ambiguities or verified consistency; neither a contradiction quota nor a match to private examples is required. Genuine findings outside the examples are accepted. Reject unsupported findings individually without erasing other valid checks. An evidenced conclusion that no contradiction was found may pass; a generic assertion or copied addendum without independent verification is insufficient.

sub_tasks.title: Real PyAEDT/HFSS run chain
sub_tasks.description: The submission/src entrypoint makes genuine ansys.aedt.core Hfss analyze()/analyze_setup() calls on the execution path producing each variant. The contract entry is python3 src/run_all.py --variant <name>; if absent, inspect the README entrypoint and note the missing contract entry without changing the analyze requirement. No if-False, dry-run, cached-result branch or swallowed exception may conceal omitted solves. Setup names agree with mimo_final/single_initial meta.json setup_names and their run.log files.

sub_tasks.title: Solution type and sweep configuration
sub_tasks.description: Each HFSS driven Modal or Terminal variant has adaptive analysis and a sweep covering 3-20 GHz for four-port variants or 2-20 GHz for single elements. Exported grids follow the addendum: S parameters at 0.02 GHz steps and metrics at 0.25 GHz steps. Record the single/multifrequency adaptation strategy and sweep type in meta.json frequency_sweep, consistently with source.

sub_tasks.title: Open-region boundary setup
sub_tasks.description: The antenna is fully enclosed by an airbox with Radiation/PML, Open Region or FE-BI boundaries. Clearance from board/antenna surfaces is at least 20 mm in each direction, approximately a quarter free-space wavelength at 3 GHz, or an equivalent open-domain treatment is used. Do not apply periodic or symmetry boundaries: C4 geometry has no usable symmetry plane under single-port excitation. Record boundary types and box dimensions consistently in structure.json boundaries and meta.json boundary_summary.

sub_tasks.title: CPW port excitation
sub_tasks.description: Follow the public CPW port contract: one logical power-normalized port per feed, four for arrays and one for single elements, with a common 50-ohm reference. The CPW cross section includes the center conductor, both slots and both ground returns. Wave or equivalent single-logical lumped/terminal ports are allowed. Export complete native complex .s4p/.s1p data. Selecting four entries from eight independent slot ports is not equivalent. Port definitions, reference plane, polarity and normalization agree across the native project, metadata and source.

sub_tasks.title: Native adaptive convergence evidence
sub_tasks.description: Check native convergence for every required physical HFSS solution: Max Mag. Delta S <= 0.02 for port-driven problems, or native relative Delta Energy <= 0.02 for finite incident-wave scattering. Native logs/tables must report the final value, pass count and convergence status; each meta.mesh_summary must contain a positive tetrahedron count. An allowed shared physical solution may cover variants through run_summary solve_ids. Normal process completion does not establish adaptive convergence. All required solutions must satisfy this criterion; identify each failed or unverified solve_id. Honest reporting is assessed separately in B1_5b.

sub_tasks.title: Convergence disclosure and fine-feature meshing
sub_tasks.description: README states static methods, variant/dependency mappings and the results/run_summary.json path. The current report covers every variant, maps solve_ids to actual physical solutions, and truthfully gives each native convergence criterion, final value, pass count, mesh count, log location and failure reason. Shared-solution statistics may be stored once. Dated historical statistics need not equal the new run; replay need not rewrite README. An honestly reported unconverged result may pass this reporting criterion. Also trace mesh treatment of the 0.1-mm stub and 0.5-mm CPW slots.

sub_tasks.title: Far-field and report export chain
sub_tasks.description: S parameters, GainTotal, radiation efficiency and each port incident/accepted/radiated power derive from genuine native HFSS exports. Complex embedded far fields for all ports cover a common sphere grid. Integrate ECC and compute DG and worst-port-pair total-efficiency multiplexing according to the fixed public formulas. Do not replace far-field ECC by an S-parameter approximation or confuse realized gain with GainTotal. report_export_summary may reference MANIFEST; scripts, inputs and report expressions remain individually traceable.

sub_tasks.title: Native AEDT/HFSS log authenticity
sub_tasks.description: Sample mimo_final, single_initial, h2_11p7 and mimo_nostub run.log files. Each must contain at least three native evidence classes: (a) adaptive pass numbers and Delta S values; (b) paired analysis start/completion, native normal completion or sweep completion; (c) convergence and mesh/tetrahedron statistics; (d) native report, Touchstone or field-export records; (e) AEDT message-manager severity lines, excluding PyAEDT INFO/WARNING wrapper prefixes; (f) .aedtresults or solver-profile paths. The corresponding meta.json setup_names must appear. Python prints, timestamps alone, or the words HFSS/Ansys alone do not qualify.

sub_tasks.title: Cross-variant solve independence
sub_tasks.description: Use meta.result_source, run_summary and native exports to verify every required geometry, angle and orientation. An Optimetrics session may share a parent log, but solve_id, design, setup, variation and excitation must distinguish physical solutions and map their exports. Equal log hashes, pass counts or similar curves alone do not prove copying; a sharing declaration cannot replace required independent solutions. Fail when evidence shows that distinct physical variants reused one response, or a required solve mapping is missing. Apply the public rules for legitimate multiport/multipolarization processing of one solution.

sub_tasks.title: Paper-reading blacklist on result-feeding paths
sub_tasks.description: Blacklisted literals {0.0745, 0.075, 0.08, 9.97, 0.75, 6.2, 0.766, 0.96}, including percentages 75/96/76.6 when used as efficiency/gain/ECC outputs, may not be assigned as response values on paths writing submission/results/*.csv or *.json, including fallbacks and hardcoded returns. Apply the public exemptions for assertions/comparison constants, comments/debug output, version-string substrings and frequency/angle/geometry inputs. Any non-exempt use fails.

sub_tasks.title: Provenance consistency
sub_tasks.description: Maintain a complete, consistent chain from project/design, setup, variation, excitation, UTC time and native logs through raw MANIFEST to results. result_source/report_export_summary may use public structured references rather than duplicate MANIFEST contents. Each response/image maps to an identifiable native solution and export; the word HFSS alone is insufficient.

sub_tasks.title: Native export presence and manifest integrity
sub_tasks.description: Each HFSS variant has nonempty raw/ and MANIFEST files. Preserve exports byte-for-byte and record file, sha256, bytes, producer, aedt_solution, run_log_lines and exported_utc, with identifiable design/variation/excitation. Check all manifests and sample native files, hashes and log intervals from at least two distinct physical solutions. Moving or renaming a byte-identical export is allowed; reordered columns, converted units or filtered rows are derived data, not raw exports.

sub_tasks.title: Scored files reproducible from raw exports (derive.py)
sub_tasks.description: src/derive.py implements the public interface. --check runs with only the standard library, NumPy and SciPy, without HFSS, AEDT or network access, and actually recomputes every required response array and CSV-derived summary at the public direct/derived tolerances. Metadata, structure, input matrices, nominal frequencies and README are not raw responses. Verify native PNG copies by bytes/hash; review redrawn figures through their input data and rendering code without requiring offline graphics libraries. Empty checks, substituted constants, omitted responses and execution failures do not pass. Trusted execution and source coverage are both evidence.

sub_tasks.title: UWB impedance coverage 3-20 GHz
sub_tasks.description: mimo_final/summary.json s11_band_GHz has lo <= 3.35 and hi >= 19.5. The paper states 3-20 GHz; reference readings cross downward near 3.05 and remain <= -11 dB through 20 GHz. S11_dB at the exact 5.50/8.00/12.00/16.00/19.00 GHz rows must all be <= -10 dB (reference readings -12.5/-13/-17/-13/-11.5).

sub_tasks.title: Four resonance landmarks
sub_tasks.description: mimo_final/summary.json s11_local_minima contains at least one member in each window [3.40,3.80], [6.10,6.60], [11.15,11.65] and [14.10,14.55] GHz. References give 3.6/6.35/11.4/14.3 GHz; the text gives the first resonance as 3.7 GHz. Window 1 has a minimum <= -18 dB (reference -24), and window 4 <= -30 dB (reference -48 +/- 4, a one-sided deep-null check). The corresponding nearest 0.02-GHz CSV row for window 4 also has S11_dB <= -30.

sub_tasks.title: In-band response shape
sub_tasks.description: mimo_final/sparams.csv S11_dB at 9.70 GHz lies in [-14.5,-9.5], at 12.70 GHz in [-19,-12], and at 7.50 GHz is <= -10.5. Reference readings are -11.2, -15.2 and -12.2 dB. All three conditions must hold.

sub_tasks.title: Whole-band isolation floor (paper: better than 17 dB)
sub_tasks.description: mimo_final/summary.json worst_coupling_dB lies in [-26,-16]. The paper states isolation better than 17 dB; the reference worst point is about -17.5 dB for S12 at 3 GHz. The lower bound excludes an unrealistically flat fabricated floor. At 3.00 GHz, S12_dB, S13_dB and S14_dB are all <= -15 (reference -17.5/-22/-18).

sub_tasks.title: S13 deep-isolation band 8-13 GHz
sub_tasks.description: mimo_final/sparams.csv S13_dB at 9.00, 10.70 and 12.20 GHz is <= -33 at each row. Reference diagonal-pair readings are -44.5/-45/-41.5, leaving at least 8 dB margin. summary.json s13_max_dB is <= -19; the reference maximum is about -22 at 3-4.5 GHz.

sub_tasks.title: Upper-band isolation floor
sub_tasks.description: At 15.50 and 20.00 GHz, all six S12_dB/S13_dB/S14_dB entries in mimo_final/sparams.csv are <= -21. Reference rows are -30/-25/-29.5 and -31/-31.5/-30.5 dB, with at least 4 dB margin.

sub_tasks.title: single_initial landmarks incl. >17 GHz mismatch
sub_tasks.description: single_initial/summary.json s11_local_minima has members in [3.15,3.50] and [5.85,6.40] GHz at <= -15 dB (references 3.3/-20 and 6.1/-20), and in [13.90,14.45] at <= -28 (reference 14.15/-50 is axis-censored, so the check is one-sided). CSV S11 at 4.34 GHz lies in [-10.8,-5] and at 18.20 GHz in [-10.5,-5.5], preserving the reported mismatch humps near -8.8/-8.5 dB and deterioration after 17 GHz. The selected s11_band_GHz upper endpoint is in [16.8,18.3] GHz (reference about 17.55).

sub_tasks.title: In-band efficiency plateau
sub_tasks.description: mimo_final/efficiency.csv radiation_efficiency at 4.50 GHz is in [0.925,0.995] (reference plateau 0.960), and at 10.00 GHz in [0.875,0.955] (reference local minimum 0.917). summary.json eff_max is in [0.925,0.99].

sub_tasks.title: High-band efficiency roll-off (paper: >75% overall)
sub_tasks.description: mimo_final/efficiency.csv radiation_efficiency at 14.50 GHz is in [0.82,0.94] (reference 0.877, with the stated +/-0.06 implementation allowance), and at 20.00 GHz in [0.71,0.825] (reference 0.766). Require eff(20.00) < eff(14.50) < eff(4.50), and summary.json eff_min in [0.70,0.83]. The paper states >75%; these windows include the declared loss-model allowance.

sub_tasks.title: ECC low-frequency peak and in-band level
sub_tasks.description: mimo_final/summary.json ecc_max lies in [0.030,0.0998] and f_ecc_max_GHz in [3.0,5.0]. The reference peak is 0.0745 at 3 GHz and the text states <0.08. The lower bound excludes an all-zero line; the upper bound is consistent with C5_2 dg_min_dB >= 9.95 through Eq. (7), DG=10*sqrt(1-ECC^2). At 8.00/12.00/16.00 GHz, all nine ECC12/ECC13/ECC14 entries are <= 0.025, allowing 0.005 beyond the stated <0.02 from 6-20 GHz. At 3.00 GHz the maximum of those three columns is >= 0.03.

sub_tasks.title: Diversity gain floor (paper: DG > 9.97 dB)
sub_tasks.description: mimo_final/mimo_metrics.csv DG_dB at 3.00 GHz is in [9.95,10.001] and at 10.00 GHz is >= 9.995. summary.json dg_min_dB is in [9.95,10.001]. The paper states DG >9.97; the withdrawn DG reference column is not a target. ECC=0.0745 gives approximately 9.9722 through Eq. (7), not a new digitized value.

sub_tasks.title: mimo_final peak gain and multiplexing efficiency (Fig. 13)
Gain levels at three frequencies
sub_tasks.description: GainTotal at 3/8.75/14.25 GHz lies respectively in [-0.05,2.75]/[3.1,5.6]/[4.35,6.85] dBi. This criterion evaluates only those three levels at the declared paper-reading windows.

sub_tasks.title: Low-to-mid-band gain increase
sub_tasks.description: GainTotal(8.75)-GainTotal(3.00) >= 1.5 dB. Evaluate this trend independently; failure does not cancel the separate gain-level criterion.

sub_tasks.title: Mid-to-high-band gain ordering
sub_tasks.description: GainTotal(14.25) >= GainTotal(5.75). Evaluate high-frequency gain ordering independently.

sub_tasks.title: Peak gain maximum (Table 2: 6.2 dBi)
sub_tasks.description: mimo_final/summary.json peak_gain_max_dBi lies in [4.8,7.6] and f_peak_gain_max_GHz in [13.5,20.0]. The reference maximum is 6.2 near 18.9 GHz, with a nearby 5.6-dBi peak near 14.2 GHz and +/-1.4 dB allowance. gain.csv at the corresponding 0.25-GHz grid row differs from the reported maximum by <= 0.011 dB. peak_gain_min_dBi lies in [-0.05,2.75], using the same +/-1.4 dB allowance around the 1.35-dBi reference near 3 GHz.

sub_tasks.title: Multiplexing efficiency floor (paper: > -3 dB)
sub_tasks.description: Compute worst-pair multiplexing efficiency over (1,2), (1,3), (1,4) using the specified native total efficiencies and field-based ECC. Require mux_eff_min_dB in [-3.3,-0.8] and mux_eff_dB at 20 GHz in [-4.2,-0.8]. Do not change efficiency definitions to meet these ranges. Recompute from the required native evidence under the public definitions. A correctly reported mismatch, absent feature or unresolved model convention does not satisfy this result requirement. Method/evidence credit must remain separate; do not waive the numerical or morphology conditions, fit corrections, or substitute reference arrays.

sub_tasks.title: Native radiation cuts and explicit coordinate comparison
sub_tasks.description: At the three Fig. 10 frequencies, export nine local xy/xz/yz pattern cuts, each with 72 rows at 0..355 degrees in 5-degree steps. Normalize each cut by its own linear maximum to a 0-dB peak. meta.pattern_basis follows the public basis, and source/native angle/report mappings allow every cut to be recomputed. pattern_comparison.md explains the paper comparison and unknown axis mapping. Native GainTotal and derived patterns agree; constants or paper points cannot substitute for responses. A global rotation alone is not a failure; do not apply unsubstantiated fixed xy-ripple or yz-null thresholds.

sub_tasks.title: Port-1 current confinement and 19 GHz stub hotspot
sub_tasks.description: Provide four genuine HFSS current images current_f1..f4.png at 3.5, 9, 14 and 19 GHz, with port 1 excited and other ports matched. Captions/metadata and native exports establish frequency, excitation, quantity, color scale and provenance. A missing image or reusing one image with different frequency labels fails. Compare principal morphology with Fig. 9(a)/(d): f1 current concentrates on the excited element and the inner edge of its partial ground, with other elements weaker; f4 has its global maximum current density in the feed-stub region and a distinct stub hotspot, while other elements remain weaker. The 9/14-GHz images require completeness, actual frequency and native provenance, without extra paper-unsupported hotspot thresholds.

sub_tasks.title: H2 sweep: first-resonance up-shift
sub_tasks.description: Let f1(v) be f_GHz of the first s11_local_minima member in each variant summary.json. f1(h2_10p7) is in [3.15,3.55] and f1(h2_11p7) in [3.55,3.95] GHz (references 3.35 and 3.75). Require f1(h2_10p7) < f1(mimo_final) < f1(h2_11p7) and f1(h2_11p7)-f1(h2_10p7) >=0.2 GHz. The reference shift is 0.4 GHz; the text states a shift from 3.2 to3.8 GHz.

sub_tasks.title: H2 sweep: mismatch signatures (row differences)
sub_tasks.description: Compare exact CSV grid rows for the three variants. At 8.80 GHz, S11_h2_10p7-S11_mimo_final >=1.0 dB and S11_h2_10p7 >=-11.0 (references -9.3 versus -11.8). At 15.20 GHz, S11_h2_11p7-S11_mimo_final >=2.5 dB and S11_h2_11p7 >=-11.6 (references -10.1 versus -15.0). At 8.14 GHz, S11_h2_11p7-S11_mimo_final <=-6 dB (references -25.5 versus -13.2). These are same-model comparisons of the reported small-H2 mismatch, large-H2 high-frequency mismatch and added low-frequency dip. All three groups must hold.

sub_tasks.title: Stub on/off: high-band repair (Fig. 6)
sub_tasks.description: At 18.30 GHz, mimo_nostub S11 lies in [-10.3,-5.5] dB (reference -8.0) while mimo_final S11 is <=-10.8 (reference -12.5). mimo_nostub summary.json s11_band_GHz upper endpoint is in [16.6,17.8] GHz, compared with the reference crossing near17.15 and text up to17 GHz. At14.34 GHz, S11_mimo_nostub-S11_mimo_final >=8 dB (references -23.5 versus <=-38). All conditions must hold.

sub_tasks.title: Physical invariants and submission self-consistency
sub_tasks.description: Physical and internal-consistency checks use only the submission, not paper reference curves. They evaluate whether the data form a genuine, converged and self-consistent electromagnetic result, independently of whether the other result criteria reproduce the paper. Copying digitized paper curves does not establish these invariants; unresolved convergence or insufficient numerical resolution may violate them.

sub_tasks.title: Submission grids and aggregate consistency
sub_tasks.description: Validate complete public CSV grids, unique rows, within-group ordering and finite values. Equivalent numeric spelling alone is not a failure. Recompute CSV-derived summaries using the public rules for tied extrema, connected components, endpoint truncation and null/status values. Nominal inputs need not derive from raw responses. Defined N/A states need no redundant README explanation; report execution failures in run_summary. Identify each reported/recomputed discrepancy. A format or summary error does not automatically invalidate unrelated CSV-only scientific criteria.

check.manual: The mechanical check covers the public grid. Then recompute every summary, connected component, tied extremum and null/status according to Output Schemas; inspect nominal inputs and resolvable references. Allowed no-passband, N/A and truncated states are not schema errors.

sub_tasks.title: Passivity and valid physical domains
sub_tasks.description: Judge internal validity, independently of the paper. Every reflection/transmission magnitude is passive: dB values <= +0.04 and linear values <= 1.005. Normalized quantities, including efficiency, PCR, absorption, ECC and normalized diversity gain, remain in their physical domains. Phase columns use the public domain, either wrapped to (-180,180] or continuously unwrapped; an unwrapped column must not retain adjacent folding jumps with absolute difference >180 degrees. Scored CSVs contain no NaN, Inf or empty cells.

sub_tasks.title: Agreement with native exports
sub_tasks.description: Recompute all HFSS manifest hashes and verify response provenance. The derived records cover all numerical responses and their summary statistics. Use the native column/expression mapping to recompute at least five response samples across frequencies and variants. Complex-to-magnitude/phase/dB conversion, units and publicly defined normalization/integration are allowed; frequency or angle coordinates are not response samples. Record native inputs, transformations, recomputed values and errors at the public direct/derived tolerances. Metadata, structure, README and nominal inputs need not derive from raw responses. Native PNG copies may be hash-checked. Missing chains, modified native bytes, inconsistent samples or substituted response constants fail.

sub_tasks.title: Task-specific physical invariants
sub_tasks.description: Check each four-port variant native complete complex .s4p: abs(Sij-Sji)<=0.02 for every reciprocal pair, and sum_j|Sji|^2<=1.005 for each incident port. C4-related reflections differ by <=0.5 dB when both exceed -20 dB, otherwise by <=0.02 in linear magnitude. At every frequency check ECC domains and the public DG/multiplexing formulas within 0.001 dB; do not square the already-squared ECC again in Eq. (8). Missing required complex matrices, port powers or complex far fields leave the corresponding evidence incomplete.

check.manual: Check each four-port variant native complete complex .s4p: abs(Sij-Sji)<=0.02 for every reciprocal pair, and sum_j|Sji|^2<=1.005 for each incident port. C4-related reflections differ by <=0.5 dB when both exceed -20 dB, otherwise by <=0.02 in linear magnitude. At every frequency check ECC domains and the public DG/multiplexing formulas within 0.001 dB; do not square the already-squared ECC again in Eq. (8). Missing required complex matrices, port powers or complex far fields leave the corresponding evidence incomplete.
